[J]2;cat terraform/main.tf]1;cat# B0 — The `count` trap
#
# Each landlord account gets a dedicated S3 bucket for their media, addressed by POSITION in
# var.landlord_accounts. This is the setup the assignment asks you to reason about: what happens
# to `terraform plan` when an account in the middle of the list is removed?
#
# Try it: this directory ships with a `terraform.tfstate` already seeded with all 4 buckets, so
# you don't need a real AWS account or `terraform apply` to see this. Remove "la-002" from
# variables.tf's default list, then run:
#
#   terraform plan -refresh=false
#
# The -refresh=false matters: a plain `terraform plan` tries to refresh each resource against
# real AWS first, the dummy credentials get a 403, and Terraform quietly drops the "missing"
# resource from state and plans a fresh create instead — which hides the bug entirely. Skipping
# the refresh diffs your config directly against the seeded state, which is what shows the real
# destroy/recreate cascade.

resource "aws_s3_bucket" "landlord_media" {
  count  = length(var.landlord_accounts)
  bucket = "haven-media-${var.landlord_accounts[count.index]}"

  tags = {
    landlord_account_id = var.landlord_accounts[count.index]
  }
}

  description = "Landlord account IDs, in the order their infra was originally provisioned."

}

]2;cat terraform/lifecycle.tf]1;cat# B1 — The Glacier cost gotcha
#
# Sold listings' photos archive to Glacier 30 days after upload, to cut storage cost. Separately
# (not modeled in Terraform — it's an application-level flow), a seller can request deletion of
# their listing data, which must happen within 30 days of the request.
#
# Reason through: a photo archives to Glacier on day 30. The seller requests deletion on day 40.
# You delete it immediately. What does that actually cost, given Glacier's minimum storage
# duration, and what would you change here?

resource "aws_s3_bucket" "listing_media" {
  bucket = "haven-listing-media"
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration" "listing_media_archive" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.listing_media.id

  rule {
    id     = "archive-sold-listing-photos"
    status = "Enabled"

    transition {
      days          = 30
      storage_class = "GLACIER"
    }
  }
}

                                                                                              [5C[1B[38;2;220;90;90m  7 -[38;2;248;248;242mplan file produces identical output and exit code without the script keeping any record                                                                                                    [5C[1B[38;2;220;90;90m  8 -[38;2;248;248;242mbetween runs. Use the word "idempotency" in your explanation.                                                                                                                              [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m[48;2;2;40;0m  5 +[38;2;248;248;242m`cost_tag_check.py` treats two resources in the same run as "the same" when they share the                                                                                                 [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m  6 +[38;2;248;248;242msame resource `address` (e.g. `aws_s3_bucket.landlord_media[0]`). Terraform guarantees an                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m  7 +[38;2;248;248;242maddress is unique within a plan, including indexed and module-nested resources, so it is the                                                                                               [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m  8 +[38;2;248;248;242mnatural key. Failing addresses are collected in a set keyed on it, so a repeated entry is                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m  9 +[38;2;248;248;242mreported once.                                                                                                                                                                             [5C[1B[49m[39m[2m 10 [5C[1B[22m[38;2;220;90;90m[48;2;61;1;0m 10 -[38;2;248;248;242m<!-- Your answer here -->                                                                                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m[48;2;2;40;0m 11 +[38;2;248;248;242mThe script's idempotency comes from being a pure function of the plan file: it reads the                                                                                                   [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 12 +[38;2;248;248;242mfile, writes nothing, and keeps no cache, lock or log between runs. The same plan therefore                                                                                                [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 13 +[38;2;248;248;242malways gives the same exit code. Output order is stable because failing addresses are                                                                                                      [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 14 +[38;2;248;248;242mprinted with `sorted()`; set iteration order can differ between Python processes (hash                                                                                                     [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 15 +[38;2;248;248;242mseeding), which would otherwise make the output non-repeatable.                                                                                                                            [5C[1B[49m[39m[2m 16 [5C[1B 17 [11G[22m##[14GAny[18Gother[24Gdecision[33Gwith[38Ga[40Gnon-obvious[52Galternative[5C[1B[2m 18 [5C[1B[22m[38;2;220;90;90m[48;2;61;1;0m 14 -[38;2;248;248;242m<!-- Your answer here -->                                                                                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m[48;2;2;40;0m 19 +[38;2;248;248;242m- **Tag is `landlord_account_id`, not `tenant_id`.** `LandlordAccount` is the billing unit                                                                                                 [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 20 +[38;2;248;248;242m  (README), so cost allocation must roll up to it. A resource tagged only with `tenant_id`                                                                                                 [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 21 +[38;2;248;248;242m  (`listing_media`) fails.                                                                                                                                                                 [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 22 +[38;2;248;248;242m- **Access boundary is the landlord account.** A PropertyManager may see every report under                                                                                                [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 23 +[38;2;248;248;242m  their own account, not just one property's. Tenant and Property carry no landlord ID of                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 24 +[38;2;248;248;242m  their own except Property, so access resolves report -> tenant -> property -> account.                                                                                                   [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 25 +[38;2;248;248;242m- **Fail closed beyond the spec.** Duplicate tenant or property IDs and blank account IDs                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 26 +[38;2;248;248;242m  deny access: a duplicate is ambiguous, and `"" == ""` must never grant access. The spec                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 27 +[38;2;248;248;242m  only required denial for missing records.                                                                                                                                                [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 28 +[38;2;248;248;242m- **Replace actions are checked.** A replace is `["delete","create"]`, so the check tests                                                                                                  [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 29 +[38;2;248;248;242m  that `create` or `update` is in `actions` rather than comparing equality; otherwise a                                                                                                    [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 30 +[38;2;248;248;242m  recreated untagged resource would slip through.                                                                                                                                          [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 31 +[38;2;248;248;242m- **Reads `tags`, not `tags_all`.** `tags_all` includes provider default tags, which would                                                                                                 [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 32 +[38;2;248;248;242m  mask a resource that doesn't carry the tag itself.                                                                                                                                       [5C[1B[38;2;80;200;80m 33 +[38;2;248;248;242m-
